## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

baseHeight(x,z) {
  const r = Math.hypot(x,z);
  const cityMask = smoothstep(500, 820, r);
  const n = this.noise.fbm(x*0.0021, z*0.0021, 5);
  const ridge = 1 - Math.abs(this.noise.fbm(x*0.0034+7, z*0.0034-3, 4)*2-1); // ridges 0..1

  // massifs
  const north = Math.exp(-(Math.pow((x-120)/1250,2) + Math.pow((z+1900)/1000,2)));
  h += cityMask * 420*north;

  // small rolling

}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world street racing game with a semi-realistic city and mountain map, smart AI traffic, multiple cars, button controls, two driving modes, and three camera modes.

## Requirements
- Include normal and drift driving modes; hood, follow, and fixed camera modes.
- Support keyboard and touch controls.
- Deliver a playable game now without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, viewport at most 1280px wide, and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Game concept and title: **Apex City — Street Drift**.
- Include free roam, city sprint, and mountain pass events, plus nitro, drift scoring, settings, and responsive mobile controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with the game canvas, loading/menu screens, event selection, HUD, touch controls, pause/settings, and results UI.
- Created `styles.css` with responsive styling for the interface, mobile controls, menus, and HUD.
- Downloaded Three.js module and fonts into local `vendor/` assets.

### Active
- Core game implementation: Three.js scene, city/mountain world, car physics, AI traffic, race events, camera modes, keyboard/touch input, and HUD wiring.

### Blocked
- No external blocker; implementation paused after a tool call failed with `upstream connection lost`.

## Next Move
1. Continue implementation by creating the core JavaScript modules, beginning with `js/main.js` and any supporting world/vehicle/UI modules.
2. Run the game locally and fix runtime or visual issues.
3. Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and verification results when finished.

- `index.html`: Game UI and canvas structure; loads `js/main.js`.
- `styles.css`: Complete game UI styling and responsive controls.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: Locally downloaded Three.js module.
- `vendor/fonts/`: Locally downloaded Chakra Petch and Orbitron font assets.

## Important Context
- `index.html` references a Three.js import map mapping `three` to `./vendor/three.module.js`, and loads `./js/main.js`.
- The game is not yet playable; UI scaffolding and assets exist, but the game logic has not been written.
- Changes are uncommitted.

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser

  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position

Save as:

  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world street racing game, **Apex City — Street Drift**, with a semi-realistic city and mountain map, AI traffic, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Validate the game in-browser and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include free roam, city sprint, and mountain pass events; normal and drift driving modes; hood/follow/fixed cameras; nitro; drift scoring; settings; and responsive controls.
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, use a viewport no wider than 1280px, and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Game title and concept: **Apex City — Street Drift**.
- Include free roam, city sprint, and mountain pass events.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI in `index.html` and responsive styling in `styles.css`.
- Downloaded local Three.js module and fonts under `vendor/`.
- Began rebuilding `js/main.js` with a Three.js import, scene/renderer, lighting, city blocks, mountain route, cars, minimap, driving, traffic, race, camera, and HUD logic.

### Active
- Finish `js/main.js`; the latest edits stop after defining `action()`, so event/menu interactions, keyboard and touch bindings, animation loop, resize handling, and startup are still missing.
- Run `node --check js/main.js`, launch/reload `http://localhost:3002`, and fix runtime or visual issues.
- Exercise menu, driving, camera and drive mode toggles, and race start; capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- Browser runtime validation is pending until `js/main.js` is completed. The earlier `ReferenceError: THREE is not defined` is addressed by adding `import * as THREE from 'three';`, but no post-change runtime check has been performed.

## Next Move
1. Complete `js/main.js` with UI event handlers, keyboard/touch input, pause/settings/restart flows, animation loop, resize handling, and startup.
2. Run `node --check js/main.js`; reload `http://localhost:3002` and inspect browser console.
3. Test the requested gameplay flows and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.
4. Summarize results and assumptions; note changes are uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: In-progress game implementation; needs completion and validation.
- `index.html`: Game UI and module entry point.
- `styles.css`: Game UI styling and responsive controls.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: Local Three.js dependency.
- `.playwright/cli.config.json`: Browser config.

## Important Context
- Earlier browser console error was `ReferenceError: THREE is not defined` at `http://localhost:3002/js/main.js:3:17`; `js/main.js` now imports Three.js, but has not been revalidated.
- The HTTP server on port 3002 was started earlier, but a later check found it unavailable; restart it if needed.
- Working tree changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world street racing game, **Apex City — Street Drift**, with a semi-realistic city and mountain map, AI traffic, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Validate the game in-browser and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include free roam, city sprint, and mountain pass events; normal and drift driving modes; hood/follow/fixed cameras; nitro; drift scoring; settings; and responsive controls.
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, use a viewport no wider than 1280px, and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Game title and concept: **Apex City — Street Drift**.
- Include free roam, city sprint, and mountain pass events.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI in `index.html` and responsive styling in `styles.css`; implemented the Three.js game, world, driving, events, HUD, controls, settings, and menus in `js/main.js`.
- Fixed duplicate `startGame` declaration and adjusted city route alignment.
- Browser-tested boot, WebGL, free-roam keyboard driving, camera and drive-mode toggles, pause/settings, and city event start; no runtime exceptions were reported.
- Captured and read the menu screenshot; captured a city-race screenshot at 1280×800.

### Active
- Inspect the latest city-race screenshot and address any visual or gameplay issues found.
- Finish remaining validation, particularly mountain event, touch controls, and race progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Read `/tmp/opencode/playwright/apex-race.jpg` as the latest screenshot.
2. Test mountain-pass start, touch controls, and checkpoint/race progression; fix any issues.
3. Re-run `node --check js/main.js` and summarize the completed work and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: Three.js scene, routes, vehicle physics, event flow, and input handling.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `styles.css`: UI styling and responsive layout.
- `/tmp/opencode/playwright/apex-race.jpg`: Latest 1280×800 city-race screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser testing used Chromium’s remote debugging protocol; the validation reported no `Runtime.exceptionThrown` events.
